Cc: security@corta.com
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 17:12:00 +0000
Subject: CAIQ scope variance & evidence tagging for third-party connectors

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. We're finishing our CAIQ review (v4.0 crosswalk) and have a couple of scope variances to confirm before we finalize the control mapping on our side. Two notes:

1) Connectors out of scope for our assessment: 
   - analytics-pipeline (deployed to partner infra for batch aggregation)
   - partner-sync (3rd-party-managed webhook sync)

2) We need evidence artifacts to be tagged in Redwood's submission so our audit team can quickly identify: data-retention controls, key-management/rotation artifacts, and runtime isolation for connectors. Ideally each artifact would include a control tag (CCM id), short description, and owner.

Can you: 
- confirm whether the two connectors above are considered out-of-scope for the CAIQ instance you'll export to us;
- add tagging metadata to the evidence binder (or point us at a template we can use if you prefer to ingest our tags);
- attach any high-level mapping spreadsheets you already have.

I've attached a short exhibit showing the scope notes on our side (corta_caiq-scope-exhibit.xlsx). Our target is to wrap this by end of next week for our internal review.

Appreciate the help — Ben

--
Ben Ellis
Senior Information Security Manager
Corta Systems
ben.ellis@corta.com

Ben —

Thanks for the clear note and the attached exhibit. Short answers up front:

- Confirmed: analytics-pipeline and partner-sync will be marked OUT-OF-SCOPE for the CAIQ bundle we produce for external reviewers. We'll include a scope statement in the export header.

- Evidence tagging: we have a lightweight CSV template we use for artifact tagging (control_id, artifact_name, artifact_type, owner, short_desc, evidence_link). I'll attach that template: redwood_evidence-tags-template.csv. If that format works for your audit team, Marissa can seed the template with the artifacts we plan to include.

Next steps I propose:
- Today: Marissa will produce an initial mapping for the in-scope services and draft tags for the most frequently requested controls (data retention, KMS, access reviews).
- Tue (2027-05-11): we deliver the tagged binder + a short mapping summary PDF and a Drive folder with the artifacts.

If that timeline is tight for you, let us know and we can prioritize the data-retention/KMS artifacts first.

Kimberly Park
Head of GRC Programs, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
